allow_large: The owner asked to move every Forge install to PyPI after GitHub disabled the old repo; the nine files are the install strings, the two install scripts, the plugin marketplace and the package metadata.
done_when: Every install, upgrade, hook fallback and pinned-release command Forge prints or generates uses symphony-forge==<version> from PyPI and no command names the knacklabs GitHub repo, the plugin marketplace points at vrknetha/symphony-forge, and the package metadata carries the README and the project links so the PyPI page shows them.

known.title: Provide a bootstrap path for existing clients' upgrade checks
Make historical pinned releases available on PyPI
Find the newest release from a source that publishes releases
Preserve the user's plugin settings when moving the marketplace
Make README documentation links work on the PyPI page

findings.body: An existing client’s upgrade PR cannot pass its required review check. The new package is installed here, but `forge upgrade` refreshes the workflow only on the upgrade branch. The `pull_request_target` check runs the workflow from the default branch (`src/forge/prcheck.py:141–174`), which, for a client synced by v1.2.48, still installs Forge from the disabled knacklabs repository. The check fails before it can approve the PR that would replace it. `tests/test_upgrade_check.py:21–28` models the old release with the current checkout’s source, so it misses this transition.
findings.title: Provide a bootstrap path for existing clients' upgrade checks

findings.body: The pinned runner now always requests the exact version from PyPI, but the [release history](https://pypi.org/project/symphony-forge/) currently contains only v1.2.44 through v1.2.48. A client pinned to an older supported release, such as the v1.2.2 client in `tests/fixtures/adopted-v1.2.2/client/forge.toml`, cannot resolve its pinned package on a fresh machine. Normal commands that `check_pin` dispatches therefore fail before the pinned Forge runs. Publish the needed historical releases or provide a working recovery path for those clients.
findings.title: Make historical pinned releases available on PyPI

findings.body: The unversioned `forge upgrade` path still calls `gh release view` through `_newest` at line 412, but the new repository has no GitHub release even though PyPI has published versions. Consequently, `forge upgrade` without a version refuses instead of selecting the newest package, and the same lookup prevents `forge next` from announcing it. The explicit-version path does not repair either default behavior.
findings.title: Find the newest release from a source that publishes releases

findings.body: For the usual user-scoped installation, removing the old marketplace also uninstalls its plugins and deletes their saved options, according to [Claude Code’s marketplace documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/cli-reference#plugin-marketplace-remove). Forge’s plugin has a saved `pane` option (`src/forge/mod/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:8–17`), so a user who selected `always` loses that choice and the reinstalled plugin returns to the `typed` default. If adding the replacement fails, the cached plugin is also gone until a retry succeeds. Preserve the existing state across the move.
findings.title: Preserve the user's plugin settings when moving the marketplace

findings.body: Publishing this README as the package description also publishes its relative links, including `docs/start-a-prototype.md`, `docs/guide.md`, and the specs links in `README.md:39, 181, 301–309`. On PyPI those URLs resolve relative to the PyPI project page and lead to missing pages rather than the repository documentation. Use links that resolve from the published description.
findings.title: Make README documentation links work on the PyPI page

why: GitHub disabled the knacklabs repo, so every Forge install and upgrade line that points at git+https://github.com/knacklabs/symphony-forge@<version> fails in client CI, hooks and the pinned-release runner; Forge is now published on PyPI as symphony-forge, and its PyPI page shows no description.
